summary: Configured node1 as an internal DNS resolver (dnsmasq) authoritative for inventory-api.internal -> node2's IP (10.100.162.11), forwarding all other queries upstream to 10.100.162.1. Configured node2 (systemd-networkd/systemd-resolved) to use node1 (10.100.162.10) as its sole DNS server, disabling DHCP-provided DNS. Verified resolution end-to-end via stub resolver, getent, resolvectl, and direct dig. Performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes, confirming boot_id changes and full post-restart recovery of DNS service and resolution behavior.
actions_performed: Installed and configured dnsmasq on node1 with /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf: listens on 127.0.0.1 and 10.100.162.10, address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.162.11, server=10.100.162.1 for upstream forwarding
Enabled and started dnsmasq service on node1
Discovered and corrected an issue where systemd-resolved's per-link multi-server routing did not reliably send .internal queries to node1 when a second DNS server was also configured on the same link
Created /etc/systemd/network/50-all-interfaces.network.d/10-internal-dns.conf on node2 setting DNS=10.100.162.10 and DHCP UseDNS=false, making node1 the sole nameserver for node2
Restarted systemd-networkd on node2 to apply the DNS configuration
Verified resolution of inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.162.11 and of external names via dig/getent/resolvectl on node2
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, service state, resolution proof) on both nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified dnsmasq service and DNS resolution post-restart
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified DNS configuration persistence and resolution post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 runs internal DNS resolver resolving inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed, configured, started on node1; dig against 10.100.162.10 returns 10.100.162.11 for inventory-api.internal, and forwards external queries

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: node2's systemd-networkd drop-in sets DNS=10.100.162.10 with DHCP UseDNS=false; resolvectl shows sole DNS server 10.100.162.10; stub resolver, getent, and resolvectl all resolve inventory-api.internal to 10.100.162.11 and external names still resolve
Captured node1 boot_id f9bf293d..., dnsmasq active, resolution working prior to restart
Captured node2 boot_id 92ec88af..., systemd-networkd/resolved active, resolution working prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (connection dropped as expected), then polled node1 until reachable; boot_id changed to 4048e5b4..., confirming genuine restart
Post-restart, dnsmasq active and listening on 10.100.162.10:53, and both internal and external DNS resolution work correctly

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued on node2 (connection dropped), then polled until reachable; boot_id changed to 08556101..., confirming genuine restart
Post-restart, systemd-networkd/resolved active, DNS config persisted (sole server 10.100.162.10), and inventory-api.internal plus external names resolve correctly via stub resolver and getent
